analysis.overall: You had a fantastic day with 96% of your time spent in range and a steady average glucose of 119 mg/dL. The only real wrinkle was a slight overnight rise that led to a gentle early morning low.

events.title: Late afternoon peak
events.description: Blood sugar gradually climbed to 185 mg/dL following afternoon meals and corrections, but a meal bolus brought it smoothly back into target within two hours.

events.title: Dinner and late snack
events.description: A 50g carb dinner was handled well initially, though a follow-up late snack around 11:20 PM contributed to a slow rise over the midnight hours.

events.title: Overnight rise
events.description: Glucose topped out around 184 mg/dL overnight from delayed carb absorption, prompting several small automated micro-corrections.

events.title: Early morning dip
events.description: The tail end of overnight correction insulin slowly pulled glucose down to 66 mg/dL, where it held flat until breakfast without crashing further.

events.title: Breakfast peak and recovery
events.description: Bolusing well for your 65g breakfast kept the spike mild, peaking at 150 mg/dL before settling right back down into a steady range.

analysis.watch_for_tomorrow: Keep an eye on late-night snacks, as late carbs can trigger overnight corrections that eventually cause early morning dips.
